_comment: Edit this file, then re-run. Nothing else needs changing.

goal._milestones_note: Optional. Delete this list and the dashboard generates a ladder scaled to your target.
goal._goal_note: volatility is yearly, used only for the uncertainty band (16% is roughly a global equity index). target_mode 'spending' derives the target from annual_spending / withdrawal_rate instead of using target. plan_to_age is how far the projection runs.

currency._note: Splits reported return into asset performance and exchange-rate movement. Only useful when your funds report in a different currency from the one you spend. Set enabled=true and asset_currency accordingly.

_targets_note: Your intended portfolio weights. Must sum to 1. Tickers with a target you do not yet hold are fine - the next-buy allocator will start building them. Rebalancing here is buy-only: it never suggests selling.
_phases_note: Your savings timeline. As many phases as you like - study, jobs, a promotion, a career break. Each phase saves either a share of its income (saving_mode 'rate', the default, using savings_rate) or a fixed amount (saving_mode 'fixed', using monthly_saving). end=null means open-ended; phases may not overlap; gaps save nothing. income_growth is real yearly growth within the phase. Amounts are real, in today's money. You can also edit all of this on the dashboard and copy it back here.
_events_note: Optional one-off lump sums: a bonus or inheritance (positive) or a big purchase (negative). date is 'YYYY-MM'.
_fund_data_note: Each fund's regional split, factor tilt and expense ratio are fetched on every refresh (weekly cache) from Vanguard's public fund data, iShares' holdings files and Yahoo Finance. Free, no account or key. Set enabled to false to rely on lookthrough below only; add tickers to extra to fetch funds you don't hold or target yet.

fund_data._emerging_note: Which countries count as emerging markets when a fund's country list is grouped: msci (Korea and Poland emerging, the usual definition) or ftse (they count as developed; the index family Vanguard's global funds follow).

_lookthrough_note: Optional overrides on top of the fetched fund data. A fund's own us/dev/em here replaces its fetched split; tilt (1 = deliberate small/value fund), ter (0.0006 = 0.06%) and role override one by one. Leave a fund out to use only what is fetched.
_basket_note: Approximate currency of the assets INSIDE each fund. USD is only the fund's reporting currency - VT holds euros and yen too. Update from fund factsheets.

pensions._note: Optional, off by default. Swiss pension pots, all in today's money. pillar2/pillar3a grow at their own real_return and are paid into the portfolio at unlock_age (3a can be drawn from 5 years before the AHV reference age of 65). AHV is a yearly pension from start_age that reduces what the portfolio must pay out. Put real balances only in your own config.json.

benchmark._note: Compared with your time-weighted return in section 04, as a total-return index (dividends reinvested), converted to display_currency when the currency section is on. Any ticker IBKR can find. Set ticker to null to hide.
benchmark._choices_note: Benchmarks fetched on each refresh, so the Settings page can switch between them instantly.

dividends._note: IBKR's feed reports dividends gross; this rate estimates tax withheld at source. 0.15 = US treaty rate with a W-8BEN on file.

_scenarios_note: Optional. Named what-ifs, each holding only what it changes from the plan above. The dashboard lists them next to your plan; its 'Copy as config' button writes this format for you.
